chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Mansur ibn Buzurj, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), while I was standing: 'May Allah make me your ransom. A partner of mine had a wife under him, so he divorced her and she became irrevocably divorced from him. Then he wanted to return to her, and the woman said: 'No, by Allah, I will not marry you ever until you make Allah a condition upon you that you will not divorce me, nor will you marry (another wife) upon me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And he did so?' I said: 'Yes, he has done so, may Allah make me your ransom.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Evil is what he has done, and he does not know what may occur in his heart in the middle of the night or the day.' Then he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'As for now, so tell him to complete for the woman her stipulation, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The Muslims are (bound) by their stipulations.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I have doubts regarding a word.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not Imran who passes by you, is he not with you in Al-Madina?' So I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So tell him to write it, and let him send it to me.'

So Imran came to us after that, so we wrote it for him, and there was neither any increase nor reduction in it. So he returned after that and met me in the flour market, so he rubbed his shoulder against my shoulder, so he said: 'He conveys the greetings to you, and he is saying to you: Tell the man to fulfill his stipulation.'

key_terms.الْمُسْلِمُونَ عِنْدَ شُرُوطِهِمْ: The Muslims are bound by their stipulations
key_terms.مُرَاجَعَتَهَا: To return to her (revocation of divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fulfilling conditions set by a wife for her husband to take her back after an irrevocable divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle that stipulations in marriage revocation (ruju') are binding provided they do not contradict the essence of the contract, reinforcing the Prophetic maxim 'Muslims are bound by their conditions.' The Imam’s instruction to document the condition highlights the practical necessity of written evidence in preventing future disputes, a key aspect of Shia fiqh regarding marital rights. It underscores that mutual consent can create additional obligations beyond the default legal framework.
